subject: Data Engineering
title: Lack of ACID in Lakes
description: A quick win: understand Lack of ACID in Lakes.

hook.text: Two jobs write to the same lake folder at the same time. One overwrites the other. Data is lost.

buildup.text: Traditional data lakes are just files on object storage. They have no transaction support.

discovery.text: Without ACID properties, concurrent writes can corrupt data, and failed writes leave partial results.

twist.text: Readers might see half-written data mid-update. There's no isolation between reads and writes.

climax.text: The lack of ACID was the data lake's biggest weakness — and the reason lakehouses were invented.

punchline.text: No transactions means no safety. Lakes needed an upgrade.

quiz.question: What does the lack of ACID properties mean for data lakes?
options: Concurrent writes can corrupt data and readers may see partial results
